[[Austin, Texas]], U.S. (operations) | num_locations = 100 (2025) | key_people = {{ubl|class=nowrap | [[Revathi Advaithi]] ([[Chief executive officer|CEO]]) | Kevin Krumm ([[Chief financial officer|CFO]]) | [[Michael Capellas]] ([[chairman]])}} | revenue = {{decrease}} {{US$|25.81 billion|link=yes}} (2025) | operating_income = {{increase}} US$1.169 billion (2025) | net_income = {{decrease}} US$838 million (2025) | assets = {{increase}} US$18.38 billion (2025) | equity = {{decrease}} US$5.002 billion (2025) | num_employees = 147,979 (2025) | website = {{url|https://flex.com}} | footnotes = Financials {{as of|2025|03|31|lc=y|df=US}}.{{cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/0000866374/000086637425000027/flex-20250331.htm|title=Form 10-K for FY 2025|publisher=[[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]]|date=May 21, 2025|access-date=July 29, 2025}} }} [[File:Flex (автор Стоялов Максим).jpg|thumb|Flex offices/warehouse in [[Łódź]]]] '''Flex Ltd.'''{{cite web|url=https://flex.com/who-we-are|title=People and Company-wide Culture|website=flex.com|access-date=11 December 2017}} (previously known as '''Flextronics International Ltd.''' or '''Flextronics''') is a Singapore-domiciled [[multinational corporation|multinational]] manufacturing company. It is the world's third{{Cite news|url=https://mfgmkt.com/httpsmfgmkt-comwp-contentuploads201704top-50-ems-companies-2016-pdf/the-mmi-top-50-press-release/|title=The MMI Top 50 Press Release|work=Manufacturing Market Insider.|access-date=21 June 2017|archive-date=5 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200405185640/https://mfgmkt.com/httpsmfgmkt-comwp-contentuploads201704top-50-ems-companies-2016-pdf/the-mmi-top-50-press-release/|url-status=dead}} largest global [[electronics manufacturing services]] (EMS), [[original design manufacturer]] (ODM) company by revenue, behind only [[Pegatron]]. Flex's U.S. corporate headquarters are located in [[Austin, Texas|Austin]], Texas.{{cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/866374/000086637423000028/flex-20230331.htm|title=Form 10-K for FY 2023|publisher=[[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]]|access-date=May 25, 2023}} The company has manufacturing operations in over 30 countries, and employs about 172,000 people. ==History== [[File:Flex US Headquarters San Jose.jpg|thumb|Former U.S. headquarters in [[San Jose, California]]]] [[File:Flextronics logo.svg|thumb|Logo used until 2015]] [[File:Destructions in Mukachevo after Russian attack, 2025-08-21 (01).jpg|thumb|The Flex plant in [[Mukachevo]], Ukraine after the Russian attack in 2025]] The company was founded in 1969 by Joe and Barbara-Ann McKenzie as Flextronics, Inc.{{Cite web|title=Making history: The rise of Flex and the technological revolution {{!}} Flex.com|url=https://flex.com/resources/making-history|access-date=2020-11-23|website=flex.com|language=en}}{{Citation needed|date=November 2020}} In 1990, the company was renamed Flextronics International, Ltd. and moved to Singapore. In 1993, the company received venture capital funding through [[Sequoia Capital]],{{cite web|url=http://www.sequoiacap.com/us/home/flextronics/info|title=Sequoia – Flextronics|website=Sequoia Capital|access-date=11 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924100635/http://www.sequoiacap.com/us/home/flextronics/info|archive-date=24 September 2015|url-status=dead}} and became a publicly held company again in 1994. In 2000, the company ranked third on "100 Best-Managed Companies" by ''[[IndustryWeek]]''. In 2006 Flextronics took over a part of the production of [[Lego]], but in 2009 Lego decided to end relations with Flextronics and purchase the production facilities in Mexico and Hungary. On 4 June 2007, Flextronics offered to purchase [[Solectron]] for [[United States dollar|US$]]3.6 billion and thus making Solectron a subsidiary of Flextronics. The acquisition of Solectron was completed by end of October 2007, earlier than anticipated. On 18 March 2009, Flextronics was invited to ring the [[NASDAQ]] stock market opening bell, signifying the day's start of trading and celebrated 15-year NASDAQ-listed anniversary. Mike McNamara (then-CEO) and a group of top executives represented the company at the ringing of the bell.{{cite web|url=http://www.companieshistory.com/flextronics-international-presentation-video/|title=Flextronics International|date=9 July 2013|website=Companieshistory.com|access-date=11 December 2017}} On 25 August 2009, Flextronics announced that it was chosen by [[LG Electronics]] (LGE), a global provider of advanced digital products and applied technologies, to manufacture 19, 22, 26, 32, and 37-inch LCD television receivers at its [[Ciudad Juárez]], [[Mexico]] facility for distribution to the North and South American markets.{{cite news|url=http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/flextronics-selected-by-lg-electronics-to-manufacture-assorted-lcd-tv-products-for-north-and-south-american-markets-62034407.html|title=Flextronics Selected by LG Electronics to Manufacture Assorted LCD TV Products for North and South American Markets|agency=PR Newswire|access-date=11 December 2017}} On 2 September 2009, Flextronics announced that Multek received [[Danaher Corporation|Danaher]] Test and Measurement's 2009 Outstanding Supplier Award. The award was given based on quality, delivery performance, engineering support and cost for work with two of Danaher's business units, [[Tektronix]] and [[Fluke Corporation|Fluke]].{{cite news|url=http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/multek-wins-danaher-test-and-measurements-2009-outstanding-supplier-partnership-award-62046182.html|title=Multek Wins Danaher Test and Measurement's 2009 Outstanding Supplier Partnership Award|agency=PR Newswire|access-date=11 December 2017}} On 15 September 2010, Flextronics announced that it had been chosen by [[Brammo]], Inc., former producer of electric traction motors and traction batteries, to be its manufacturing partner for the production and distribution of plug-in electric motorcycles and components. In 2010, the company signed an agreement with [[Lenovo]] to provide manufacturing for Europe. That same year, Flextronics also signed an agreement with Brammo to provide acquisition and manufacturing in North America, Asia and Europe. In 2012, Flextronics incubated [[Elementum]], a start-up supply chain management (SCM) company based in Mountain View, California. In 2014, Elementum was spun off from Flextronics as its own separate entity.{{cite web|url=https://blogs.wsj.com/venturecapital/2014/02/04/flextronics-spins-off-startup-to-put-supply-chain-software-in-the-cloud/|title=Flextronics Spins Off Startup to Put Supply Chain Software in the Cloud|first=Deborah|last=Gage|date=4 February 2014|website=The Wall Street Journal|access-date=11 December 2017}} In 2013, Flextronics began making the [[Mac Pro]] for [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] in Texas.{{Cite news |last=Nicas |first=Jack |date=2019-11-21 |title=No, That Mac Factory in Texas Is Not New |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/20/us/politics/trump-texas-apple-factory.html |access-date=2026-03-18 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} In 2014, Flextronics was named as the manufacturer of the Fitbit Force by the US Consumer Product Safety Commission in the context of a complete recall of the product due to rashes developing on the wrists of its users.{{cite web|url=http://www.cpsc.gov/en/Recalls/2014/Fitbit-Recalls-Force-Activity-Tracking-Wristband/|title=Fitbit Recalls Force Activity Tracking Wristband - CPSC.gov|website=Cpsc.gov|access-date=11 December 2017}} In July 2015 the company announced it changed the company name from Flextronics to Flex.{{cite news|url=http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/flextronics-officially-changes-name-to-flex-300118268.html|title=Flextronics Officially Changes Name to Flex|date=24 July 2015|agency=PR Newswire|access-date=9 January 2017}} In September 2015, Flex acquired [[Nextpower]] (then known as Nextracker), one of the leading [[solar tracker]] companies, for $330 million.{{Cite web|title=Flextronics: A Quiet Giant In Solar|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/michaelkanellos/2015/09/08/flextronics-a-quiet-giant-in-solar/|last=Kanellos|first=Michael|website=Forbes|language=en|access-date=2020-05-12}} In November 2015, Flex, acquired [[Wink (platform)|Wink smart home platform]] to bring the Intelligence of Things "Home". Flex has been a strategic partner to Wink, serving as their primary supplier of hardware and firmware, including the Wink Hub and Wink Relay, which include core intellectual property developed within Flex.{{cite news|url=http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/flex-to-bring-the-intelligence-of-things-home-with-wink-acquisition-300179504.html|title=Flex to Bring the Intelligence of Things Home with Wink Acquisition|agency=PR Newswire|access-date=11 December 2017}} In July 2017, Flex sold Wink to i.am+ for $38.7 million.{{cite web|title=i.am+ buys Wink, the smart home hub formerly owned by Flex and Quirky|url=https://techcrunch.com/2017/07/27/i-am-buys-wink-the-smart-home-hub-previously-owned-by-flextronics/|last=Lunden|first=Ingrid|date=July 27, 2017|website=Tech Crunch|access-date=February 1, 2019}} On 31 December 2018, Michael M. McNamara resigned as the company's Chief Executive Officer.{{cite web |url= https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/flex-ceo-mike-mcnamara-to-retire-300738236.html |title= Flex CEO, Mike McNamara, to Retire |date= October 25, 2018 |website= prnewswire.com|access-date= February 1, 2019}} On 11 February 2019, Flex announced [[Revathi Advaithi]] as CEO. Prior to Flex, Advaithi was president and chief operating officer for the Electrical Sector business for [[Eaton Corporation]].{{cite web|url= https://flex.com/newsroom/press-releases/flex-announces-revathi-advaithi-as-ceo |title= Flex Announces Revathi Advaithi as CEO |date= February 11, 2019 |website= flex.com|access-date= February 11, 2019}} On August 21, 2025 a Flex manufacturing site operating in [[Mukachevo]], Ukraine, since 2012 was hit and extensively damaged by a [[Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian airstrike]].{{Cite news |last=Myre |first=Greg |date=2025-08-21 |title=Russian airstrikes hit a U.S. factory in western Ukraine |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/08/21/g-s1-84146/russia-ukraine-american-factory |work=NPR |language=en}} ==Controversies== ===Breach of contracts=== Flextronics was sued for breach of contract with Beckman Coulter Inc., a maker of medical devices. The case dates from 1997, when Beckman Coulter entered into an agreement with Dovatron, a unit of the Dii Group, to provide circuit boards for a Beckman blood analyser. Flextronics acquired the Dii Group in 1999 and, according to Beckman, shortly thereafter Flextronics refused to provide the circuit boards unless it bought other electronic components from the company. Beckman filed suit in early 2001, seeking $2.2 million in damages, which were cited as the costs incurred in having to retool one of its plants to manufacture the circuit boards in-house.{{cite web|url=http://www.callahan-law.com/Verdicts-and-Settlements/Callahan-Blaine-Wins-934-Million-for-Beckman-Coulter.shtml|title=Callahan & Blaine Wins $934 Million for Beckman Coulter|website=Callahan & Blaine|access-date=11 December 2017}}{{cite web|url=http://www.mddionline.com/article/california-jury-awards-beckman-coulter-934-million|title=California Jury Awards Beckman Coulter $934 Million|date=1 November 2003|website=Mddionline.com|access-date=11 December 2017}} At the end of the trial, Flextronics paid $23 million for the damages.{{cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10698823666934400|title=Flextronics Will Pay $23 Million To Beckman to Settle a Lawsuit|first=Scott|last=Thurm|date=28 November 2003|access-date=11 December 2017|website=The Wall Street Journal}} ===Leak of USB charger confidential shipment data=== A former Flextronics executive pleaded guilty to committing wire fraud and security fraud by providing confidential information related to USB charger shipment data used for U.S. based iPhones and iPods in 2009.{{cite news|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/apples-weak-link-on-secrets-contract-equipment-manufacturing/|title=Apple's weak link on secrets: Contract equipment manufacturing? – ZDNet|first=Larry|last=Dignan|work=ZDNet|access-date=11 December 2017}} ===Seizure of Huawei goods over tariff war=== According to a 2019 report, Flex produced smartphone and 5G base stations for Huawei, and when the US added Huawei to its Entity List on May 16, Flex kept Huawei's assets at its factory in Zhuhai. This included production equipment, raw materials, and half-made products worth approximately 700 million yuan ($101.85 million).{{cite web |last1=Jiang |first1=Sijia |title=Exclusive: China's Huawei seeks compensation from Flex over withheld goods |url=https://www.euronews.com/2019/08/06/exclusive-chinas-huawei-seeks-compensation-from-flex-over-withheld-goods |website=Euronews |date=6 August 2019 |publisher=Reu |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210509054116/https://www.euronews.com/2019/08/06/exclusive-chinas-huawei-seeks-compensation-from-flex-over-withheld-goods |access-date=11 May 2023|archive-date=9 May 2021 }} These goods were held up for over a month, however Huawei was able to retrieve some of the goods worth 400 million yuan through third-party channels in June 2019.{{cite news |last1=Jiang |first1=Sijia |title=Electronics maker Flex 'seized' $100 million of Huawei goods in China: Global Times |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-huawei-tech-flex-idUSKCN1UK1C9 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220427194252/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-huawei-tech-flex-idUSKCN1UK1C9 |access-date=11 May 2023 |archive-date=27 April 2022 |work=Reuters}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category|Flextronics}} *{{Official website|https://www.flex.com}} {{Finance links | name = Flex Ltd. | symbol = FLEX | sec_cik = 866374 | yahoo = FLEX | reuters = FLEX.O | google = FLEX:NASDAQ }} {{Major OEMs}} {{S&P 500 companies}} [[Category:Electronics companies of Singapore]] [[Category:Electronics companies established in 1969]] [[Category:Singaporean companies established in 1969]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Nasdaq]] [[Category:1980s initial public offerings]] [[Category:Multinational companies headquartered in Singapore]] [[Category:Tax inversions]] [[Category:Electronics manufacturing companies]] [[Category:Electronics companies of the United States]]
extract: Flex Ltd. (previously known as Flextronics International Ltd. or Flextronics) is a Singapore-domiciled multinational manufacturing company. It is the world's third largest global electronics manufacturing services (EMS), original design manufacturer (ODM) company by revenue, behind only Pegatron. Flex's U.S. corporate headquarters are located in Austin, Texas. The company has manufacturing operations in over 30 countries, and employs about 172,000 people.
